ratings_why.fun: Every turn asks which Lids are fuel and which are savings, and the Doorward, Slit-Mender, Past Master and Worshipful Master chains reward planning, though long cascades risk being hard to follow.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: Lids don't count as the front row, so a row of doors sends enemy attacks into a back-row punisher, and Underneath plus Usher let you hide other tribes' units. No tribe today fights with a board it doesn't show.

verdict_why: The v3 rule fixes made the fight order readable; what's left is edge timing and tuning, so more versions would change the design without improving it.

points.text: An Under-Chamber Sexton under a durable top unit never opens, so it becomes an eighth Patient unit for Mabyn and Diadem. It's a great off-label use; keep it.
Gossamer Jill fills the empty slots that Pardo's Nieces and the Sexton's summons need. That clash is a real build choice; keep it rather than smoothing it out.
Usher on a Hunter or Mire tank is the best cross-tribe trick here. A second Lid-giver at Tier 5 that picks the Knock would grow that build.
The Worshipful Master's count Knock has no knocker, so its own Spring hits a random front-row enemy. Aiming it at the enemy with the most Attack would make the capstone moment land.
Patience against Spring is the best decision in the tribe, and the Ballot Clerk now pays on both. One more card that pays on both sides would make hybrid boards a real third path.

standouts.why: Re-closing a Lid turns any Spring into a repeatable one; it combos with Slit-Mender, Corkhinge and the across Knocks.
Breaks the seven-slot limit and reads the dead unit above; works with Oozes, Bog tanks and Patience.
Puts any tribe's unit under a Lid, which opens up the most surprising boards.

weakest.why: A plain across-Knock body; it does its one job and nothing else.
A small Patient seed with no hook into the Spring side.
Grows only while shut and opens on a count; fine, but it doesn't interact with other cards.

flags.note: Slit-Mender with Corkhinge and the Past Master stabs the enemy across before each attack, growing each time and staying untargetable. The only answer is what you put across from it.
Mabyn's gain grows with the square of Patient units; with Diadem, an Underneath Sexton and a golden copy it could run away on a win streak.
If the Slit-Mender has closed its Lid again, does the Worshipful Master's replay Spring it from under the Lid, and does it close again afterwards?
